overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by not making draft open session minutes available within 10 days of a request; the minutes' accuracy was upheld.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to provide February 19 open session minutes within the 10-day period required after a May 6 request.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to make the draft minutes available within 10 days of the request, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the February 19 minutes were inaccurate, misattributing a statement between members and misrecording the chair's remarks.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the minutes are sufficiently accurate to comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The AG noted the Committee did not send the complaint to the AG and report remedial action within 14 business days, and reminded it of its obligations.
allegations.key_passage: As a final matter, we note that the Committee failed to respond to the complaint within the time frame required by law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
